answer: A concrete defense is stake-bonded identity: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and its reputation grows on that bond like a vine on a trellis. To run many sybils an attacker must post a separate bond for every identity, so there is no free ledge to perch extra fakes on and no crowded wharf where unpriced clones slip in. Any agent caught colluding gets its stake slashed, so the attack cost is N locked bonds plus the forfeited capital, scaling linearly with the number of fake agents instead of being near zero.
